availability_evidence: Revised annual report pages 101, 104 and 144 state that the revised financial statements were approved by the Board on 23 August 2019; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 5.6% to £202.4m and adjusted operating profit 12.4% to £15.4m, with statutory operating profit rising to £15.2m. Chain return on sales improved to 11.2%, but Torque Transmission return on sales fell to 8.1%. Net debt and leverage increased during factory investment and restructuring, although leverage of 1.29x and interest cover of 10.0x remained comfortably within covenants. Revised accounts also disclosed an intentional Gears misstatement and strengthened control remediation.
already_announced_exclusion: STEP 2020 projects, the Jintan factory move, Singapore office closure, announced redundancies, other disclosed factory moves or closures and remediation arising from the revised accounts are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Divisional margin weakness, higher debt, continuing restructuring and the serious control failure create moderate pressure. Group revenue and profit growth, improved Chain margins and ample covenant headroom provide strong offsets.

availability_evidence: Annual report pages 61, 118, 121 and 164 state that the financial statements were approved by the Board on 16 July 2021; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Continuing revenue fell 12.7% to £165.3m and adjusted operating profit to £11.2m from £13.4m during Covid disruption, while adjusted operating margin declined only 30bps to 6.8%. Operating cash flow rose to £24.9m from £9.5m, net debt nearly halved to £18.4m and leverage fell to 1.0x. The major restructuring programme was declared complete and no restructuring charge was recorded, although the group retained net liabilities and a substantial pension deficit.
already_announced_exclusion: The completed STEP 2020 restructuring, disclosed headcount reductions and site closures, temporary Covid closures, covenant revisions, pension-deferral arrangements and other announced pandemic-response actions are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: The sharp pandemic-era revenue and profit decline creates moderate pressure, but resilient margins, exceptional cash generation, much lower debt, covenant headroom and completion of the existing restructuring programme are strong contrary evidence.

availability_evidence: Annual report pages 108, 111 and 152 state that the financial statements were approved by the Board on 11 July 2023; issuer-hosted report bytes are hash-preserved locally.
observation: Revenue rose 26.6% to £247.1m, adjusted operating profit 58.2% to £24.2m and return on sales 200bps to 9.8%, with record performance, order intake growth and a strong order book. Net debt rose to £29.8m after the YUK acquisition, but the underlying business generated net cash, second-half debt reduced and leverage remained only 0.9x with substantial covenant headroom and liquidity. Operating cash flow remained strong at £17.3m despite inflation and supply-chain pressure.
already_announced_exclusion: The YUK acquisition and integration, previously announced site closures, STEP 2 cost and efficiency investments and the disclosed refinancing of facilities are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Record revenue, profit and margins, a strong order book, low leverage and underlying cash generation provide very strong contrary evidence. Acquisition-funded debt growth and residual supply-chain and inflation pressure create only limited forward pressure.
